claim: Apple's Services gross margin declined from 76.7% in FQ2 2026 to 75.6% in FQ3 2026 due to a mix shift, even as overall and product gross margins rose on tariff refunds.
stance_target: Services segment margin quality is deteriorating independent of the tariff-refund effect that flattered overall margins
scope_conditions: Apple Services segment, FQ2 to FQ3 2026
quoted_support: "Services gross margin declined from 76.7% in Q2 2026 to 75.6% in Q3 2026, caused by a different mix."

claim: CFO Kevan Parekh attributed the Services growth deceleration from 16.3% (Q2 2026) to 12.1% (Q3 2026) to the absence of a major theatrical film release (the prior year's F1) compared with prior quarters, alongside App Store revenue records despite mobile-gaming headwinds and business-model changes in selected countries.
stance_target: quantifies the precise magnitude and stated drivers of Services deceleration
quoted_support: "An analyst highlighted the sequential decline in services growth from 16.3% in Q2 2026 to 12.1% in Q3 2026. CFO Kevin Parekh attributed the decline to the absence of a major theatrical film release... Revenue from the App Store delivered a June quarter record despite mobile gaming headwinds and business model changes in selected countries."
region: selected countries (unspecified) plus global App Store

claim: Apple guided FQ4 2026 Services revenue growth to 'low teens' percent, alongside total company growth of 9-11% and iPhone growth in the mid-teens.
stance_target: forward Services growth guidance, relevant to the required-CAGR falsification test
quoted_support: "Revenue in the September quarter is expected to grow between 9% and 11% year-on-year despite foreign exchange headwinds. iPhone revenue is anticipated to grow in the mid-teens... Services revenue is expected to grow in the low teens."
